title: RawArtifactAvailable
description: Event emitted by platform-control when a raw artifact has been durably stored and is ready for downstream processing.

storage_path.description: URI or path to the stored raw artifact. This is the artifact's transport: the event notifies that the artifact exists, consumers read the bytes from here. The acquisition envelope at this URI carries the document body (#707).

content_type.description: MIME type of the stored artifact.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the artifact was created.

metadata.description: Optional provider-specific metadata captured with the artifact - what describes the artifact, never the artifact itself. The inline document body (`inline_body` / `inline_body_base64`) is deliberately omitted here and replaced by `inline_body_omitted: true`, so event size stays bounded by the metadata rather than scaling with the document. Inlining it made a 1.44 MB federal act exceed the NATS `max_payload` and drop out of the corpus (#707); read the body from `storage_path` instead.

inline_body_omitted.description: Present and true when the captured resource had an inline body that was stripped from this event. Its absence is stated rather than implied, so a consumer never has to guess whether the provider captured nothing.
